FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
A large truck or RV requires more stopping distance than a car at the same speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
In the manual’s 55-mph comparison, an average car stops in about 400 feet while a large truck may need almost 800 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Do not pull ahead of a big truck and abruptly slow or stop; it may be unable to stop before striking you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Trucks and RVs need extra turning room and may swing wide for a right turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
Before passing a large vehicle you are following, inspect its turn signals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
If a truck appears to turn left, pause and recheck its signals because it may actually be setting up a right turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A01
A truck’s elevated seat and large mirrors do not eliminate its broad blind areas, called the NO ZONE. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A01
Stay out of truck blind spots; an unseen vehicle could be struck if the truck swerves around a hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A01
As a general cue, if the truck’s driver is invisible to you in its side mirror, the driver cannot see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A01
Do not cut into a truck’s or RV’s forward space to reach an exit or turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A01
Avoid driving alongside a truck or RV because it may need that space to avoid a road hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A01
The handbook directs passing trucks and RVs on their left, then moving ahead rather than lingering in a blind spot. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A01
Do not tailgate a truck; its driver may not know you are close behind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A01
A large truck or RV may appear to be traveling slower than its actual speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0030]
